subject: How to join a dataframe and spatial dataframe without a region

messages.author: 4ddc99c6029ba75d
messages.subject: How to join a dataframe and spatial dataframe without a region
parts:
Hi:
This is not a reproducible example but I would provide a link to the
shapefile if needed.
I am trying to merge a dataframe and a spatial dataframe but they
don't have
a common column to do it. I wonder if someone can shed some light on
how to
accomplish this task. This is what I have:

library(spsurvey)
library(rgdal)
dsn=paste(getwd(), "/luck_ash.shp",sep="")
luck.map <- readOGR(dsn=dsn, layer="luck_ash")
names(luck.map)
[1] "perint" "strahcat" "length_km"

# Convert luck.map to dataframe and then join to shp so it can be
plotted with ggplot2
luck.mapDF <- as.data.frame(luck.map);head(luck.mapDF)
gpclibPermit()
shp <- fortify.SpatialLinesDataFrame(luck.map,region= " ") # Don't
know what to use for region
head(shp)
long lat order piece group id
1 -2128642 2722289 1 1 0.1 0
2 -2128630 2722338 2 1 0.1 0
3 -2128611 2722369 3 1 0.1 0
4 -2128571 2722483 4 1 0.1 0
5 -2128528 2722541 5 1 0.1 0
6 -2128390 2722639 6 1 0.1 0

# After using fortify.SpatialLinesDataFrame I don't have a common
column to join 'luck.map' and 'shp'
> names(shp)
[1] "long" "lat" "order" "piece" "group" "id"

names(luck.map)
[1] "perint" "strahcat" "length_km"

shp2 <- join(luck.map,shp,by="??????");head(shp2)
ggplot(shp,aes(long,lat,colour=id)) + geom_line()

messages.author: 45a85351148578ad
messages.subject: RE: How to join a dataframe and spatial dataframe without a region
parts:
Hi Felipe,

I guess you can use the id created by fortify to "merge" the result to the
original data.frame ("luck.mapDF"). This id would correspond to row number
in this data.frame (e.g. the number of each feature; you can use something
like luck.mapDF$id <- 1:dim(luck.mapDF)[1]). After this, you can plot the
lines, but remember to set a "group" aesthetic (for instance id or group as
resulting from fortify).

Hope this helps,
fernando

messages.subject: Re: How to join a dataframe and spatial dataframe without a region
parts:
It might be easier if you work with segments. maptools and spatstat can
help.

For example, this will mark the intermittent / perennial streams

require(maptools)
require(spatstat)
require(ggplot2)

poly = readShapeLines("luck_ash")
poly.psp = as.psp.SpatialLinesDataFrame(poly)
poly.streams = poly.psp$ends
poly.streams$int = poly.psp$marks
ggplot(poly.streams) + aes(x=x0,y=y0,color=int) +
geom_segment(aes(xend=x1, yend=y1))

messages.subject: RE: How to join a dataframe and spatial dataframe without a region
parts:
Hi Mark,

My guess was based on that fortify outputs the id of the lines, which is
derived from the *.shx file of the shapefile, and sp gets the data.frame
part of the SpatialLinesDataFrame from the *.dbf (also the rest of things
which Felipe tried to fortify). The IDs are derived from the order of the
items, so I do not think something can be easily missed or confounded by sp
or ggplot2 ... I do not think there could be here the same problems as with
polygons and holes, for instance. Correct me please if I'm wrong.

Indeed you are right with your question, and probably I should have
indicated that this was more workaround than anything. The approach using
maptools and spatstat is in this in respect clearest and more elegant.

All the best,
fernando

parts:
I think the solution is robust only if id comes from the line slot
"ID" in the SpatialLinesDataFrame. So after a little reverse
engineering I convinced myself that this is indeed the case! (The magic
happens in ggplot2::fortify.Lines.)

The row.names of the data are just as reliable as a key to join on:

luck.mapDF$id = row.names(luck.mapDF)

(which is equivalent to your sequencer, but maybe a little more intuitive)

So your solution looks to be as robust as the relationship model of the
shapefiles (which has been very well tested by now).

Thanks!

Mark


For posterity:

###
### joining shapefile polylines to their data for nice ggplot2 plots
###
require(ggplot2)
require(rgdal)
luck.map<- readOGR(dsn=".", layer="luck_ash")
luck.mapDF<- as.data.frame(luck.map)
shp<- fortify.SpatialLinesDataFrame(luck.map)
luck.mapDF$id<- row.names(luck.mapDF)
shp2<- join(shp, luck.mapDF)
ggplot(shp2,aes(long,lat,colour=perint,group=group)) + geom_path() + coord_equal()


###
### for those that prefer the attributes to be
### attached to segments and don't mind losing
### polyline grouping information
###
require(maptools)
require(ggplot2)
spatialLines2segmentsWithData = function (poly)
{
require("spatstat")
apsp = as.psp(as(poly, "SpatialLines"))
segments=apsp$ends
segments$id=apsp$marks
d = poly@data
d$id = row.names(d)
return(merge(segments,d))
}

segmentsWithData = spatialLines2segmentsWithData(readShapeLines("luck_ash"))
ggplot(segmentsWithData, aes(x0,y0,color=perint,xend=x1,yend=y1)) + geom_segment() + coord_equal()
